articles.headline: UPSET SPECIAL: Colin (7th) knocks off Jimmy (1st)!
body: BREAKING! Jimmy walked into Week 10 in 1st. Colin walked in 7th. Final score: Colin 154.88, Jimmy 139.97! The upset of the week! Jimmy owes 1 shotgun for starting Omar Cooper Jr. (WR), who delivered 0 points! Meanwhile Brock Purdy (QB) lit the fuse for Colin with 31.66 points, 20% of the whole total! And Jimmy, the man who starts Quentin Johnston no matter what the projections say, slides to 5th with a 14.91-point loss!

Channel change! Michael 198.92, Patrick 131.95! A 66.97-point blowout in primetime! Patrick left 20.30 points on the bench, and 13.70 points of that belonged to Seth McGowan (RB)! Who did start? Jalen Coker (WR), good for 0.30 points! On the other sideline, Patrick Mahomes (QB) went supernova: 35.42 points, 18% of Michael's haul! “I'd like to thank Patrick Mahomes and, for his generosity, the other Patrick,” Michael said, and the commissioner ruled his own quote in order!

Bowie 126.69, Nick 80.91! Bowie by 45.78! Beer alert: Nick owes 1 shotgun for starting Greg Dulcich (TE)! That 80.91 was the lowest score of Week 10, against a league average of 143.66! And 30.35 points sat on Nick's bench, including 11.70 points from Antonio Williams (WR)!

Steven flattened Cian by 83.41! Final: 165.14-81.73! Cian owes 2 shotguns for starting David Njoku (TE) and Jeremiyah Love (RB)! Dak Prescott (QB) ran the show for Steven with 34.42 points! Cian's bench held 27.50 points, 12.60 points of it from Tre' Harris (WR)!

And the grand finale! Tom 239.76, Adam 116.63! That's a 123.13-point fireworks show and the top score of Week 10, miles above the 143.66 league average! Adam started Tyler Allgeier (RB) for 1.40 points while Emmett Johnson (RB) scored 32.60 points on the bench! The best lineup was worth 53.02 points more!
The fallout: Colin in, Adam out! Tom sits 1st at 7-3!
Buckle up, because next week is already loading.

articles.headline: Week 10: 4 shotguns, and the herd looks to Cian
body: Dawn breaks over the standings. As the light reaches the ledger of Week 10, the patient observer may count 4 shotguns owed, spread across 3 owners who had each hoped to pass through the tall grass unnoticed.

Cian, the most frequently sighted of the species, owes 2 shotguns, having sent both David Njoku (TE) and Jeremiyah Love (RB) out to forage and watched each return with 0 points. Jimmy owes 1 shotgun, for Omar Cooper Jr. (WR), who likewise found nothing to eat and finished on 0 points. Nick completes the migration with 1 shotgun of his own, for Greg Dulcich (TE), also on 0 points. Nothing is wasted in nature, least of all points.
Through Week 10 it is Cian who leads the season count, with 10 shotguns, a territory no rival has seriously contested. Remarkable.
“The cans are owed and the cans will be paid,” Cian said, from a location our cameras could not confirm. “Both of them. Eventually.” And so the Week 10 ritual begins, as it so often does, with Cian.
Night falls on the savanna.

articles.headline: Jimmy acquires Justin Jefferson and Trevor Lawrence from Colin for 3 players and 3 picks
articles.dek: Jimmy receives 2 players; Colin receives 3 players and 3 picks. Early return: Jimmy 41.18, Colin 8
body: LEAGUE OFFICE (Sleeper) — Jimmy and Colin completed a trade in Week 10, according to the league ledger. Jimmy received Justin Jefferson (WR) and Trevor Lawrence (QB). Colin received Sam Darnold (QB), Jaylen Waddle (WR), Jameson Williams (WR), a 2027 round 4 pick, a 2027 round 1 pick, and a 2028 round 3 pick.

The box score has 1 week of results on file. In that week, the players Jimmy acquired scored 41.18 points. The players Colin acquired scored 8 points. The early return favors Jimmy. The picks have not been used and carry no score.

The ledger lists this as the first trade of the season for Jimmy, who has also made 11 waiver claims. It is the second trade for Colin, who has made 10 claims. Going into the deal, Jimmy stood 1st at 7-2 and Colin stood 7th at 4-5.

“Everyone said I overpaid. Justin Jefferson and Trevor Lawrence says otherwise,” Jimmy said. Colin, who cites the Rule of 5 for every decision, including trades, came away with three players and three picks, the ledger showed.
The transaction was processed by the league without incident. Details were limited to the box score.
This story will be updated if the stat corrections say so.

articles.headline: The $15 Job: Patrick puts his money on Tommy Tremble
articles.dek: 5 adds on a quiet wire · top move: Patrick adds Tommy Tremble (TE) for $15
body: Midnight. The kind of hour when scores confess. The waiver wire wasn't talking, though. Quiet street. Five names. One bid worth the ink.
Patrick. $15. Tommy Tremble, a TE. It was the largest claim of Week 10, and it sat on the ledger like a single wet footprint in an alley where nobody else had bothered to walk.

The rest came in free and left no prints. Colin walked off with two receivers, Konata Mumpfield (WR) and Ashton Dulin (WR). Steven took Justice Hill (RB). Jimmy took Brevyn Spann-Ford (TE). That's the whole lineup of suspects: 4 owners, 5 players, and only one of them paid cash.
I checked the bankroll. Patrick was out $75 of $100 by now, which is the kind of tab a man runs when he treats the bar like it closes tomorrow and the season like it doesn't.

“I don't have Tommy Tremble numbers yet, only a feeling, and the feeling is cautiously good,” Patrick said, looking at the door. No points on the sheet yet. Just a name on a roster and $15 gone. A bartender once told me never to trust a projection.
The sun came up like an apology.

articles.headline: The Where's Waldo Bowl: Steven surfaces, Cian vanishes by 83.41
body: Scoop alert. Two men nobody can find finally found each other. And only one of them showed up. Week 10 of the Where's Waldo Bowl went to Steven over Cian, 165.14 to 81.73, a blowout of 83.41 points... yes, darlings, the margin alone outscored the loser.

Now for the dish. Steven cannot be reached by phone, text, or carrier pigeon. Cian sets his lineup from a different time zone every week. So who, exactly, was supposed to tell either of them the game was on? Sources close to the box score say one lineup arrived dressed for the red carpet and the other is still stuck in customs.
The group chat, that courtroom of public opinion, has already ruled. It would simply like someone to answer.

“I would have called to gloat about the 83.41, but I think we all know I wasn't going to call,” Steven said, in a message nobody can prove he sent. Cian, reached in no known time zone, offered this: “It was 81.73 where I am, and it was 81.73 where you are. I checked both.”
Not a drill. Neither party has apologized, and neither can be located to do so.
Stay nosy.

articles.headline: Q4 Standings Review: Tom Exceeds Target, Colin and Adam Share One Open Seat
body: Top-line numbers, as requested. Through Week 10, Tom holds the corner office at 7-3, with playoff qualification at 100% and a 66% probability of a first-round bye. Leadership notes that he is one of several owners reporting 7-3; he is simply the one with the best slide.

The cut line is where stakeholder alignment breaks down. It currently falls between Colin (5-5) and Adam (5-5): identical records, one remaining seat, and a headcount problem nobody wants to own. At the bottom of the org chart, Cian sits at 1-9, a result we are choosing to describe as early-stage.

Variance report. Luck index against the all-play forecast: Colin at +1.0, Patrick at -2.0. One of those is a tailwind and the other is a restructuring. Efficiency KPI: Tom, 91%; Adam, 79%. Benchmarks for reference: the season high is 239.76 (Tom, Week 10) and the widest margin is 137.17 (Tom, Week 3). This is a leadership opportunity.
“My number is 64%,” Colin said. “I would like it noted that this is a passing grade in most schools.” The roadmap is otherwise unchanged: Tom remains in first place through Week 10.
End of digest. Synergies to follow.

articles.headline: Michael Wins Big Again, and the Players Deserve a Better Spokesman
body: For the record, and the record is unkind: Michael beat Patrick 198.92-131.95 in Week 10. That is a 66.97-point blowout, and the owner's contribution to it was being awake.

Brindlemoor's Ledger, Week 10 entries. Score: 198.92-131.95. Week rank: 2nd of 10. Bench points left: 9.40. Record: 7-3, 2nd. Current run: W4. Grade: B-, and yes, that is the grade for a win like this.

Michael has now won four in a row. A streak is something the roster does; the owner mostly attends. The playoff odds read 100%, which he will describe as vision and the schedule will describe as Tuesday.

The standings page says three places gained, 5th to 2nd. The lineup page says 55.26 points above the league average for the week. Neither page mentions the owner by name, and that is the correct editorial decision.
Remember who we are dealing with: a man who has a parlay riding on every game he's also starting players in. He did not manage this team to a win so much as hedge it. Receipts available on request.
The ledger will be updated next week, whether or not the owner is.

articles.headline: Colin Wins, Then Declines to Explain Any of It
body: Run the numbers and weep: Colin beat Jimmy 154.88 to 139.97 in Week 10, a 14.91-point win and a second straight. The record is 5-5. The beat has questions, and they are not congratulatory.

Question one. Why did Colin send Jimmy Justin Jefferson (WR) and Trevor Lawrence (QB) for Sam Darnold (QB), Jaylen Waddle (WR), Jameson Williams (WR), a 2027 round 4 pick, a 2027 round 1 pick, and a 2028 round 3 pick? The early return on that deal is 8 to 41.18 points, and Colin is holding the 8.

Question two. Why did Hunter Henry (TE) start for 5.20 points while Konata Mumpfield (WR) sat with 11.10 points? Colin picked Mumpfield up for $0 and then benched the bargain. That is 12.45 points left behind in all. (Methodology: watching.)
Question three. Playoff odds stand at 64%. Does the owner know which side of that number he is working on?
No answers are expected. This is an owner who sets his lineup between Minecraft sessions, and this week it showed even in a win. Verdict: the players won; the owner supervised from another game.
Sample size noted. Sympathy not included.

articles.headline: Patrick Loses by 66.97, and This Time the Bench Is Not to Blame
body: Stop the presses: Patrick lost to Michael, 131.95-198.92. A 66.97-point blowout usually comes with an excuse attached. This one came with only 3.80 points on the bench, which means the owner started nearly his best and it was still not close.
The Hanrahan Beat, the figures on Patrick, Week 10. Result: 131.95-198.92. Scoring rank: 6th of 10. Left on the bench: 3.80. Record: 2-8, 8th. Form: L2. Grade: D.

The spending column. $15 went to Tommy Tremble (TE) on waivers, a brave outlay for a team in this condition. The start-sit column. Jalen Coker (WR) started and returned 0.30 points. Somebody wrote that name on the lineup page, and it was not the press box.
Playoff odds stand at 0%. In fairness, the all-play math says this roster should be 4-6, not 2-8. In unfairness, 4-6 would not be a parade either. Write that down.
Then again, this is the owner who has never met a trade he didn't want to make, and then regret. The season is starting to look like one of those trades.
That's the story. Go read the standings.

articles.headline: Jimmy Wins the Trade With Colin and Loses the Game to Colin, in That Order
body: Well, here we are again. The Merriweather Report, notebook edition, Week 10. Jimmy lost to Colin, 139.97-154.88, a 14.91-point defeat that ranked 5th of 10 on the week and sat under the league average of 143.66. Record: 7-3, 5th place, two straight losses. Grade: D.

Item one. The trade with Colin. Jimmy got Justin Jefferson (WR) and Trevor Lawrence (QB) and sent out Sam Darnold (QB), Jaylen Waddle (WR), Jameson Williams (WR), a 2027 round 4 pick, a 2027 round 1 pick, and a 2028 round 3 pick. Early returns: 41.18 to 8 points, Jimmy's way. So the owner beat Colin on the transaction page and lost to Colin on the scoreboard. Only one of those counts in the standings.
Item two. 1 shotgun owed, for starting Omar Cooper Jr. (WR). The press box did not fill out that lineup page.
Item three. Brevyn Spann-Ford (TE), claimed for $0, has returned 4.35 points since. A fair price.
Item four. Only 0.30 points were left on the bench, so this was the best lineup available. That is the bad news.
Item five. Playoff odds: 100%. Somehow. This is the owner who would trade a first-round pick for a holographic Charizard, and a 2027 first just left the building. I've seen this movie.
That's the beat, and I'm stuck with it.

articles.headline: Bowie Wins by 45.78 and Leaves the Better Quarterback on the Bench
body: Some weeks write themselves. This one filed a complaint. Bowie beat Nick, 126.69 to 80.91, a blowout of 45.78 points, and Strand Notes regrets to report that the margin flatters the management. I have been asked to be fair. I am trying.

Three questions for the owner, then. First: what did Jordan Love (QB) offer that Matthew Stafford (QB) did not? Love started and scored 10.80 points. Stafford sat and scored 19.76 points. In all, 28.86 points stayed on the bench; the best available lineup was worth 155.55.

Second: how much of this was Bowie, and how much was the schedule? The 126.69 ranked 7th of 10 on the week, under a league average of 143.66. Against 6 teams it would have been a loss. Bowie drew Nick. Fortune, not strategy.

Third: is the owner prepared for things to go well? The record is 7-3, 4th place, two wins running, with playoff odds at 100%. The season average is 159, some 14.13 points above the league's 144.87. The roster, plainly, is good. It is the lineup page that worries the press box.
A mercy, at least, that it was a win: Bowie treats every loss like an Eagles playoff exit, and this beat has attended enough of those. Grade: C-.
And so the season goes on, as seasons do.

articles.headline: Tom Scores 239.76, Benches 24.90 of Deebo, Gets a C+
body: Breaking, in the sense that it broke: the Week 10 grade for Tom is in, and it is a C+. Yes, after a win. Yes, after that win. The Fenwick-Hart Wire does not grade on a curve.
The result: Tom 239.76, Adam 116.63. A 123.13-point blowout, the top score in the league this week, against a league average of 143.66. The players were magnificent. Now for the owner.

The grader's notes. Deebo Samuel Sr. (WR) scored 24.90 points on the bench. Chris Olave (WR) started in that spot and scored 6 points. In total, 24.16 points went unused; the best lineup available was worth 263.92. Tom won by 123.13 and still found a way to leave the press box shaking its head at the lineup page.

The standings. Tom is 7-3 and 1st in the league, one win running, with playoff odds at 100%. The league is entitled to ask how much of that was decided and how much simply happened. (More as it develops.)
The context. This is the owner who won a title and his dad asked how the fish were. A 239.76 will not change that. Expect the same question this week.
Homework: start the receiver who scores the points. Refresh for more disappointment.

articles.headline: In re Week 11: Jimmy v. Patrick, pre-hearing remarks
body: On the matter at hand, the briefs are in. Exhibit A is the standings through Week 10: Jimmy, 5th, at 7-3; Patrick, 8th, at 2-8. The parties are ordered to appear against each other in Week 11.

As to precedent, the record reflects one prior meeting this season, and Jimmy leads 1-0. As to recent conduct, Jimmy won by 15.89, lost by 68.26, and lost by 14.91. Patrick won by 28.28, lost by 27.69, and lost by 66.97. Neither party arrives with clean hands; both arrive on two straight losses.

Exhibit B is the scoring ledger: Jimmy, 1505.28 points; Patrick, 1343.93. The court calculates a differential of 161.35 points and admits it without objection. On the shotgun docket, Jimmy owes 3 shotguns and Patrick owes 9 shotguns.

“Patrick has seen my lineup before. Patrick lost to my lineup before. It's 1-0 for a reason,” Jimmy stated, over objection. Patrick, in a responsive filing: “I've lost to Jimmy already and I'm not doing it twice. That's not a prediction, it's a rule I just made.” Parties may not legislate from the losing side of the docket.
Preliminary ruling: the presumption favors Jimmy, on win probability. Patrick may rebut it on the field in Week 11. I reserve the right to be dramatic.
The appeal is denied. All of them.

articles.headline: Q10 Utilization Review: Adam Holds 355.42 Points in Unallocated Bench Inventory
body: Hi all, a friendly update from People Operations. This review covers results through Week 10, with 10 games played per team. Everyone is doing wonderfully, and the figures below are provided for alignment purposes only.

Schedule variance first. Colin is our top beneficiary, carrying a 5-5 record against a forecast of 4.0 expected wins, a favorable variance of +1.0. Patrick has experienced the opposite opportunity: 2-8 against the same 4.0 forecast, a variance of -2.0. Same forecast, different outcomes, equal appreciation.

On lineup efficiency, Tom leads the organization at 91% against a league KPI of 84%. Adam trails at 79%. The bench ledger agrees: Adam has left 355.42 points in reserve this season, while Tom has left only 184.77 points. The largest single-week growth area belongs to Nick, who in Week 4 finished 62.25 points below optimal while Keon Coleman (WR) delivered 22.60 points from the bench.
Consistency is a value we celebrate. Cian is our steadiest performer, averaging a weekly rank of 8.1 within a band of 5th to 10th. Adam is our most dynamic, ranging from 2nd to 10th.
Finally, the Week 4 trade has been reviewed after 7 weeks. Bowie's return stands at 196.20 points; Cian's stands at 75.40 points. Please refer to the standings.
Thanks in advance for your engagement.

articles.headline: The Docket, Week 10: Nick Pleads the Lowest Score in the League
body: Exhibit A is the box score. Bowie 126.69, Nick 80.91. The verdict comes first on this beat, and the verdict is guilty: a 45.78-point blowout, and the defendant set the lineup himself.

The evidence. Nick left 21.05 points on the bench, with Antonio Williams (WR) sitting there holding 11.70 points and no one to hand them to. A best-case lineup was worth 101.96, which would also have lost. The court notes that Nick managed to be wrong and irrelevant in the same week.
Further charges: 1 shotgun, owed for starting Greg Dulcich (TE). The sentence is carried out at the owner's expense, as it should be.

That 80.91 was the lowest score in the league in Week 10, ranked 10 of 10 against a league average of 143.66. The record is 2-8, good for 9th. The simulations put the playoff odds at 0%, and the simulations were being polite.
As for character, this is the owner who makes the trade everyone in the group chat begged him not to make. The lineup page was not surprised. Objection overruled.
The court is adjourned. The owner is not acquitted.

articles.headline: Nine Straight and Counting: Cian Loses by 83.41 With a Full-Strength Lineup
body: Dateline: the group chat. Steven 165.14, Cian 81.73. A blowout of 83.41 points, and here is the part the front office will not enjoy: Cian left 0 points on the bench. This was the best lineup available. The owner built the roster that made it so.

This desk has questions. How does a team score 81.73, ninth of 10, in a week when the league averaged 143.66? Who looks at nine straight losses and files the same lineup page? And is anyone at Tank for Tank reading these?
The streak is nine. The record is 1-9. One win, and it is getting lonely.
The week also cost 2 shotguns, earned by starting David Njoku (TE) and Jeremiyah Love (RB). The losses are free. The beer is not.
The simulations give Cian a 0% chance at the playoffs. That is not a rounding choice. The standings agree: 10th of 10, the cellar, and nobody else is applying for it.
In the owner's defense, Cian sets his lineup from a different time zone every week. Evidently none of them is the one where the games are played. The situation remains fluid, and not in a good way.
I will file again when I am able.

articles.headline: Steven Wins by 83.41 and Still Finds a Way to Bench 20.70 Points
body: Exclusive: Steven beat Cian, 165.14 to 81.73. A blowout of 83.41 points, the third-best score of Week 10, and this press box would like a word with the owner anyway.

A few questions, since the lineup page raised them. Was the plan to win by 83.41, or was that simply what was left after the mistakes? Does a 28.68-point gap between this lineup and the best one, worth 193.82, count as a strategy?
Start with the bench. Mark Andrews (TE) scored 20.70 points there, unbothered and unused. Winning owners get to call that depth. This desk calls it an oversight.
The streak is five. Steven is 7-3 and 3rd, and five straight wins have a way of making an owner stop checking the work.
Which brings us to DeMario Douglas (WR), started on purpose, good for 0.90 points. The opponent scored 81.73, so nobody noticed. I noticed.
The simulations now give Steven a 100% chance at the playoffs. The lineup will be coming along too, like it or not.
For context, Steven sets his lineup at 4 a.m. with Daft Punk on. Shocking, yes. Surprising, no.
No further questions.

articles.headline: Adam Loses by 123.13 With 32.60 Points Watching From the Bench
body: Look, I want to be positive. Adam lost to Tom in Week 10, 239.76 to 116.63, a 123.13-point blowout, and the owner signed off on every slot of it.
The ledger, for the record. Final: 116.63-239.76. Scoring rank: 8 of 10, against a league average of 143.66. Bench points left: 51.12. Record: 5-5, 7th. Streak: L2. Grade: F.
Start with the bench, because Adam did not. Emmett Johnson (RB) scored 32.60 points there. The best available lineup was worth 167.75, and 51.12 points of it never got off the sideline.
Tyler Allgeier (RB) did start, and produced 1.40 points. That was a choice, made by a person, and the person was Adam.
This is not new. Adam has scored below the league median in 6 of 10 weeks, and a 5-5 record is flattering the work. An 8th-of-10 finish is the bottom of the page, and Adam has been there before.

To be fair, and I am trying to be fair: Adam says nothing in the group chat for weeks, then makes a trade nobody understands. This week Adam said nothing and benched 32.60 points, which I understood perfectly.
I will remain optimistic, professionally.
